rationale: Recover core understanding of the HashiCorp raft (Go) implementation: describe the formation/advancement line and the authority/term-context line from read source, and explain how the two connect. The map name cites the actual owner/handlers observed in raft.go, commitment.go, fsm.go, replication.go, api.go and snapshot.go; both core paths are grounded and the connection is the term fence on entries plus the startIndex commitment restriction and the ErrLeadershipLost sweep on step-down.

feedback.answered: The initial two-line question is answered for this implementation: decisions form as (index,term) log entries replicated by per-peer goroutines, and advance only when commitment.recalculate finds a quorum voter match at or beyond the leader's term startIndex; authority is a durable per-instance term plus at most one persisted vote, and context is adopted from any higher-term RPC. The connection is the term on every entry, the startIndex commitment restriction on prior-term entries, the ErrLeadershipLost answer to pending futures on step-down, and the rollback of an uncommitted configuration when a follower truncates a conflicting suffix.
remaining: No defect is asserted yet; the map records where pending support and authority interact but does not evaluate whether any interaction is unsafe.

One sourced lead worth a bounded investigation: in appendEntries a conflict at an index at or below configurations.latestIndex resets only the latest configuration to the committed one, while the committed configuration and the commitment object are untouched; what a follower in that state advertises to a subsequent RequestVote or what a subsequent AppendEntries with a configuration entry does was not traced.

Client-contract completion (A7): a future enqueued on applyCh that is never committed relies on a caller-supplied timeout; whether the library itself owes any completion for an admitted-but-uncommitted command was not established.
